title: AI in primary schools: when it starts, which tools, and what safeguards apply
asked: MPs asked what safeguards and longitudinal studies exist for early AI use in primary school, what prerequisite skills and entry point apply, what the rollout roadmap and approved tools are, what teacher training and workload support will be given, and what parents are told about data and fairness when students misuse AI.
asked_by: Dr Charlene Chen, Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat and Mr David Hoe
response: Mr Desmond Lee said AI literacy begins at Primary 1, but schools will not assign work requiring direct AI use until Primary 4, when students use only MOE-designed educational AI tools under teacher supervision. These include the AI Learning Assistant in the Student Learning Space, which redirects students who go off-topic or ask to be spoon-fed answers. From Primary 4, students also take a mandatory 10-hour "Code for Fun" programme, with optional five-hour "AI for Fun" modules. Data from MOE-built AI tools is anonymised and not used to train external AI models, national exams remain proctored with AI prohibited, and teachers receive training on ethical and pedagogical use.

key_points.point: From Primary 1 to 3, learning is physical and hands-on, and no work requiring direct AI use is assigned.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: schools will not assign any work that requires them to use AI directly.

key_points.point: From Primary 4, students use educational AI tools under teacher supervision.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: We will therefore let them use educational AI tools under teacher supervision.

key_points.point: Primary 4 to 6 students use only AI tools in school that are specifically designed for education.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: Students in Primary 4 to 6 will only use AI tools in school that are specifically designed for education.

key_points.point: Example given: Primary 4 English Language students use the AI Learning Assistant (LEA) in the Student Learning Space for composition writing in class.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: Primary 4 students in an English Language class can use the AI Learning Assistant (LEA) in SLS for composition writing in class.

key_points.point: The LEA has a guardrail that redirects students who go off-topic or ask irrelevant questions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: the LEA will redirect students back on track if they veer off-topic and ask irrelevant questions

key_points.point: From Primary 4, students take a mandatory 10-hour "Code for Fun" programme covering coding, computational thinking and an introduction to AI.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: From Primary 4, students undergo the mandatory 10 hours "Code for Fun" programme

key_points.point: Data from students' use of MOE-built AI tools is anonymised and not used to train external AI models.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: Data from students’ use of MOE-built AI tools is anonymised and not used to train external AI models that power these tools.

key_points.point: National exams remain proctored and AI use is prohibited.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: National exams continue to be proctored and use of AI is prohibited.

key_points.point: A longitudinal study, SG-LEADS by A*STAR, will start collecting data in 2027 on children's AI usage and its effects on learning and well-being.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: Singapore Longitudinal Early Development Study (SG-LEADS) by the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), which will start to collect data in 2027

key_points.point: Teachers are given opportunities to learn about AI, including ethical and pedagogical considerations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: we provide opportunities for our teachers to learn about AI, including the ethical and pedagogical considerations of its use

key_points.point: If an AI tool carries an age restriction, it will not be used for children below that age.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: If the tool has an age restriction, then we will not use it for children below that age.

key_points.point: AI tools in MOE schools are not used for social-emotional learning or to check on students' well-being.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
key_points.quote: AI in MOE schools is not used for affective or social emotional issues or social emotional learning

left_open: What procedural fairness applies when students are penalised for inappropriate AI use
Whether a study will specifically examine AI's impact on vulnerable children and those from at-risk families
What workload support teachers will receive in connection with AI use in classrooms
How the Ministry will assess readiness for any broader rollout of AI tools in schools
Whether teachers may ask primary school students to use publicly available AI tools for homework
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered cognitive offloading, parental consent and opt-outs, equity for disadvantaged students, and AI and intellectual property rights.
